name: Cologne Bonn Airport
before:
One airport for Cologne and Bonn, in the district of Porz, 12 km south east of Cologne and 16 km north east of Bonn. It passed 10 million passengers in 2024, its first year above pre-pandemic levels, and is seventh largest in Germany for passengers and third for cargo.

The round the clock licence is what sets it apart. This is one of very few 24 hour airports in Germany, which is why it is a hub for FedEx Express and UPS Airlines as well as for Eurowings.

There are three runways across 1,000 hectares, and the whole site sits within the Wahner Heide nature reserve.

It is worth knowing what else is here. The airport hosts the training centre for the German and European astronaut programmes, part of the European Space Agency, and the German Aerospace Center's old A300 ZERO-G aircraft, which used to fly zero gravity research, now stands outside near Terminal 2 as an interactive museum exhibit.

The airport is named after Konrad Adenauer, a Cologne native and the first post-war Chancellor of West Germany.
after:
One airport for Cologne and Bonn, in the south of Cologne and 16 km north east of Bonn. In 2025 it handled 10.1 million passengers, still more than 2 million short of 2019. It is sixth in Germany for passengers and third for cargo.

Round the clock opening is what sets it apart. The airport says it is the only one in Germany where UPS, FedEx and DHL all run a hub.

There are three runways across about 1,000 hectares.

It is worth knowing what else is here. Next door, on the German Aerospace Center's site, is the European Space Agency's astronaut centre, where Europe's astronauts train.

The airport is named after Konrad Adenauer, a Cologne native and the first post-war Chancellor of West Germany.

ESA's page answered a plain 403 and was read with grabb.mjs, as the brief allows.
